title.en: Godzilla Minus Zero is incredibly loud. Who decides on the cinema volume? And is it safe?

hook.en:
Godzilla Minus Zero’s incursion into Australian cinemas is proving to be a proper theatrical event.

Audiences aren’t just seeing the beast; they are feeling him. One IMAX attendee reported getting 90 decibel (dB) noise alerts on their smartwatch, and described it as the loudest film they’d ever watched.

sections.body_en:
As blockbuster soundtracks become increasingly sophisticated, the same question keeps cropping up: why are some cinema screenings so much louder than others?

The answer is a mix of artistic intent, acoustic science, industry standards and a cinema’s individual choice.

One of the key elements of film sound is dynamic range: the difference between the quietest and loudest parts of the soundtrack. Imagine two characters whispering, perhaps with some subtle ambient noise – then all of a sudden there’s an explosion.

Cinema soundtracks have a much wider dynamic range than we’re used to getting from our TV or laptop speakers.

But apparent loudness isn’t just a function of peak levels. A soundtrack with music, dialogue and effects all going at once will seem much “louder” than one with just a few very loud moments – even if the peak levels on both are the same.

Our ears also respond differently to different frequencies. Highs can be piercing, while lows can be felt in the chest.

A creature the size of Godzilla is interesting to work with. How can a sound designer convey the sheer scale of such a beast? Volume alone isn’t enough.

Large things onscreen – such as machines, thunder and beasts like Godzilla – tend to be accompanied by low-frequency sounds such as deep rumbles. Cinema subwoofers reproduce these low frequencies so you can feel them as vibrations.

Higher frequencies add detail and definition to a scene – such as the sudden crack of a building coming down, or the hit of an explosion.

The original 1954 Godzilla roar was achieved by dragging a glove coated in resin across double bass strings. Composer Akira Ifukube developed an effective orchestral language for the creature, with low frequencies suggesting mass, sharp impacts suggesting force, and reverb used to emphasise scale.

Godzilla Minus Zero joins a small number of films made for IMAX in recent years.

In 2025, at least 14 films were specifically “filmed for IMAX”, compared with the 122 films released in IMAX theatres worldwide.

This distinction matters. Films that are made for the IMAX format have enhanced presentation, including enhanced sound. Some IMAX with Laser theatres have 12-channel sound systems (including overheads and extra side channels). That can make a real difference to experiencing a character like Godzilla.

Deep bass gives the monster’s footsteps a tangible presence, while surround sound can place falling debris, explosions, and other environmental effects around you – rather than just in front.

Films are mixed in dedicated dubbing theatres, where sound engineers balance dialogue, music and effects. The traditional calibration uses a reference level of about 85dB for a test signal played through a single front speaker. This reference ensures consistent playback across cinemas. **Filmmakers and studios mix audio to industry standards**, yet cinemas are not legally bound to preserve that volume. They routinely adjust levels based on audience comfort, acoustics and business logistics.

**Smartwatches detect high sound levels**, but they cannot measure the overall sound level of a film. Hearing damage depends on sound intensity and exposure time. Sound becomes dangerous at a sustained level of 85 dBA and above. Prolonged exposure at or above 85 dBA leads to permanent noise-induced hearing loss. Cinemas manage volume levels to ensure they do not exceed legal thresholds.

Technologies like Dolby Atmos and IMAX multi-channel give directors greater control over sound. If a film is constantly loud, contrast is lost. A quiet musical gesture or subtle environmental sound can be far more disturbing than an explosion. **Godzilla’s roar succeeds through build-up**, rather than sheer volume alone.

summary.vi: Các bộ phim chiếu rạp hiện đại ngày càng sử dụng âm thanh có dải động rộng và tần số thấp để mang lại trải nghiệm mạnh mẽ, ví dụ như tiếng gầm của Godzilla. Tuy nhiên, các rạp chiếu không bắt buộc phải tuân theo một mức âm lượng cố định mà thường xuyên điều chỉnh tùy theo không gian và khán giả. Mặc dù âm thanh lớn có thể khiến người xem lo lắng về thính giác, các rạp vẫn luôn kiểm soát để đảm bảo không vượt quá giới hạn an toàn pháp lý.

en: Check online reviews before a screening to see if audiences report excessive volume levels.
Select seats toward the middle or rear rows where sound pressure levels are generally more balanced.
Pack a pair of standard earplugs in your bag just in case the theatrical mix feels too intense.
vi: Kiểm tra đánh giá trực tuyến trước suất chiếu xem khán giả có phàn nàn về mức âm lượng quá lớn hay không.
Chọn ghế ở các hàng giữa hoặc phía sau nơi mức áp suất âm thanh thường cân bằng hơn.
Mang theo một cặp nút tai thông thường trong túi đề phòng trường hợp bản phối tại rạp quá dữ dội.
